operations.exact_before: 1.1 Reindexing by $n\mapsto n+1$ is a linear isometry from $\ell^2(I,\mathbb R)$ onto $\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$, so [F7] makes $X=Y$ Hilbert spaces. All coordinates below are indexed by $j\ge1$. The truncation $A_Ne_j=2^{-j}e_j$ for $j\le N$ and $A_Ne_j=0$ for $j>N$ has finite rank, so [F3] makes it compact. Also $\|A-A_N\|=\sup_{j>N}2^{-j}=2^{-(N+1)}\to0$, so [F4] makes $A$ compact. For every $x\in\ell^2$, [F8] gives $\|Ax\|^2=\sum_{j\ge1}4^{-j}|x_j|^2\le\tfrac14\|x\|^2$, with equality at $e_1$; thus [F5] gives $\|A\|=1/2$ and $0<\omega=1<2/\|A\|^2=8$. The data norm is $\|y^\delta\|^2=\delta^2\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}2^{-j}=\delta^2$. [F3, F4, F5, F7, F8, given, algebra]
operations.exact_after: 1.1 Reindexing by $n\mapsto n+1$ is a linear isometry from $\ell^2(I,\mathbb R)$ onto $\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$, so [F7] makes $X=Y$ real Hilbert spaces, hence Banach spaces. All coordinates below are indexed by $j\ge1$. Define $(Ax)_j=2^{-j}x_j$ and, for $N\in\mathbb N$, $(A_Nx)_j=2^{-j}x_j$ when $j\le N$ and $0$ otherwise. These coordinate formulas are linear, and [F8] gives $\|Ax\|^2=\sum_{j\ge1}4^{-j}|x_j|^2\le\tfrac14\|x\|^2$ and $\|A_Nx\|^2=\sum_{1\le j\le N}4^{-j}|x_j|^2\le\tfrac14\|x\|^2$, so both maps are well-defined bounded linear operators. The range of $A_N$ is exactly the span of the ordered list $(e_1,\ldots,e_N)$: the coordinate formula gives containment, and $A_N(2^je_j)=e_j$ for $1\le j\le N$. This list is linearly independent by its coordinates, hence is an ordered basis of the range; when $N=0$ the range is $\{0\}$ with empty basis. Thus [F3] makes each $A_N$ compact. The same coordinate estimate on the tail gives $\|A-A_N\|\le2^{-(N+1)}$, with equality at $e_{N+1}$, so [F5] gives $\|A-A_N\|=2^{-(N+1)}\to0$. With Countable Choice from [A1], the Banach target and bounded linear limit just verified, [F4] makes $A$ compact. Equality in the bound for $A$ at $e_1$ gives $\|A\|=1/2$ by [F5], so $A\ne0$ and $0<\omega=1<2/\|A\|^2=8$. The data norm is $\|y^\delta\|^2=\delta^2\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}2^{-j}=\delta^2$. [A1, F3, F4, F5, F7, F8, given, algebra]
